calls.head: The Blue Jackets will send their checkers at Kucherov
calls.body: At home, the Blue Jackets keep sending Coyle’s line (Sillinger, Coyle and Olivier) out against opponents’ first lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Rick Bowness has been using this group as a checking line on the other team’s top line. Tonight the Lightning’s first line is Hagel, Cirelli and Kucherov.

story.head: Hagel has two goals and an assist as the Lightning take down the Blue Jackets
paras: Brandon Hagel opened the scoring for the Lightning early in the first. Matthew Knies made it 1-1 for Columbus on the power play midway through the period, but the Blue Jackets didn’t score again. Midway through the first, Mathieu Olivier and Scott Sabourin fought, and Ryan Lomberg and Jeffrey Viel dropped the gloves. Tampa Bay had a goal taken off for a high stick late in the second, but it didn’t cost them in the end. The Blue Jackets’ Sean Monahan didn’t play after 19:31 of the second period. Jake Guentzel put the Bolts ahead for good early in the third, in his 700th NHL game. Hagel scored again later in the period to make it 3-1. He added an assist for a three-point night.

The chances were close to even, so this one could have gone either way. The Blue Jackets hit two posts and the crossbar and still lost. Dennis Hildeby made 28 saves for the Lightning, and Jet Greaves stopped 25 of 28 at the other end. By our Swing measure, Nikita Kucherov had the best night of anyone. The Lightning moved to 13-4-2 and climbed into first in the Atlantic, while the Blue Jackets dropped to 7-10-0, still last in the Metropolitan.

items.text: The Blue Jackets are on a three-game losing streak.
